# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding**: no documented first-touch-to-first-class journey (risk of inconsistent experience, lost conversion)
- **Churn/cancellation handling**: no proactive win-back or offboarding protocol (leakage unmanaged)
- **Member check-ins**: no cadence or script for engagement/retention touchpoints (reactive only)
- **Coaching quality assurance**: no audit checklist or observation framework (standards drift)
- **Coach development**: no roadmap for progression, upskilling, or performance management
- **GDPR & member data privacy**: critical gap in a women-only studio handling personal/body data
- **Referral programme**: no operational runbook (leaving money on table)
- **Supply chain**: no process for ordering stock, equipment, or consumables (ad-hoc purchasing)
- **Incident & complaints**: no formal logging, response, or resolution protocol
- **Transformation tracking**: no SOP to capture and showcase member outcomes (marketing + retention gold)

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Coach SOPs (20/24)**: likely missing detail on class debrief, member scaling cues, 1-on-1 posture checks—critical for quality consistency
- **Client SOPs (23/33)**: gaps suggest missing cancellation, pause, milestone celebration workflows; check if member goal-setting is documented
- **Marketing (5/5)**: only 5 SOPs; missing referral ops, win-back campaigns, outcomes publishing—these drive membership growth
- **Facilities (5/6)**: minor but check cleanliness/safety audits and equipment maintenance schedules are granular
- **General (1/1)**: only 1 SOP in catchall; likely missing finance (invoicing, refunds, payment disputes), HR basics

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO ADVICE

## REVENUE — INCREASE IT NOW

• **Pricing uplift is overdue.** You're at £120–172 ARPU; November hit £170 with 107 members profitably. June dropped to £120 ARPU despite 147 members — that's a £50/month-per-member revenue leak. Audit your mix: are you selling too many low-tier memberships post-relocation? Implement a tiered pricing model (entry £35–40/month, premium £55–60) and migrate existing members up 10% by August.

• **Churn spiked to 5.74% in May and 6.6% in March; June recovered to 0% but only because you had zero cancellations.** Install a retention lever: 90-day onboarding for new members (post-relocation cohort especially), early-warning system for quiet class-goers, and a £200/year loyalty bonus for 12-month locks. Target: hold attrition at <2%.

• **The bigger studio (2x capacity) should unlock new revenue lines immediately.** You now have 147 members in a doubled space — room for 200+. Launch: (1) small-group PT packages (4-person sessions, £12–15pp/class), (2) nutritional workshops (£20/head, monthly), (3) kids/teen off-peak drop-in classes (weekend mornings, sister/partner demographics). Test the first by July.

---

## EXPENSES — CONTROL THE BLEED

• **Non-people costs are your danger zone.** Jan–April they surged from £8.2k to £30.5k (April was fit-out, understood), but they're *still* at £9.4k in June vs. £4.3k in November. That's a £5k structural increase post-move. Audit: rent, utilities, supplies, insurance, software. Rent at new studio should be 15–20% of revenue (~£2.6–3.3k); if you're over £3.5k, renegotiate or it'll choke profit. Negotiate supplier terms (cleaning, equipment, towel services) — you now have 147 members, volume should earn discounts.

• **Payroll is creeping up** (June: £3.7k vs. September baseline: £2.8k). You've added capacity; confirm headcount matches the 147-member revenue base. If you're over 4 FTE, model if a part-time shift restructure saves £300–500/month without killing service.

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your ACTUAL offerings, not aspirational ones**
- Audit what your coaches are *currently delivering* (don't guess). Spend 2 hours shadowing sessions and ask coaches: "What are the three things you deliver every session?" This prevents menu-reality gaps that confuse members and frustrate staff.

**2. Price backwards from your unit economics, not competitor rates**
- Calculate: monthly fixed costs ÷ target member count = minimum monthly revenue per member needed. Then map: what tier of service justifies that price? (E.g., "Group classes + 2 coach check-ins" vs. "unlimited personal training"). Price for *your* gym's margins, not Belfast's market average.

**3. Create TWO menus, structured completely differently**
- **Members' menu**: Outcome-focused language ("Gain strength in 8 weeks," "Build habit consistency"). Pricing tiers, what they GET.
- **Coaches' menu**: Service-delivery checklist (warm-up protocols, programming frequency, feedback cadence). This becomes your delivery standard—prevents "The Forge experience" from varying by coach.

**4. Test the member menu with 5 actual members this week**
- Share draft + pricing. Ask: "Would you pay £X for this?" and "What's confusing?" One conversation reveals more than you think. Iterate before printing/publishing.

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO REPORT
## Action plan based on live data (Dec 2025–Jun 2026)

---

## 🔴 REVENUE — BIGGEST PRIORITY

**Revenue is flat-to-declining and Rev/member has collapsed from £138 (Apr) to £118 (Jun).** This is your primary leak.

- **Pricing & upsells are underperforming.** You've grown headcount (+13 members Dec→Jun, +12% baseline) but revenue *down* 8% over the same window. This means: (a) new joiners are on lower tier memberships, or (b) existing members aren't upgrading to PT/classes/products. Audit your onboarding — are new members (Jun churn is good at 3.3%) being sold into premium tiers? Fix this first: one PT package sale per fortnight would add £200–300/month profit.

- **May churn spike to 12.7% is a red flag.** You recovered in Jun (3.3%) but lost 17 members gross. Exit interviews: are people dropping because of price sensitivity, class timetable gaps, or studio transition disruption? If it's timetable, map attendance by class and fill dead slots with higher-priced off-peak beginner or speciality classes.

- **Rev/member target: restore to £130+.** You hit £138 in Apr (pre-move), £132 in Dec. Currently £118 (Jun). That's £12/member gap × 134 members = **£1,608/month leakage.** Recover this by: (i) pricing annual memberships 5% higher on renewal (£12–15/month per member), (ii) launching a £15/month add-on (e.g. monthly wellness workshop, nutrition plan, locker access) — conservative uptake of 20 members = £300/month.

---

## 💰 EXPENSES — SECONDARY FOCUS

**Staffing and variable costs are trending high relative to flat revenue.**

- **March outflow (£23,328) and April (£39,015 planned move aside) suggest payroll or supplier invoicing spikes.** Jun outflow (£20,644) is still 31% of revenue — sustainable only if you're building cash reserves or clearing payables. **Get a 12-month supplier payment calendar.** Are you paying quarterly utilities, insurance, or rent upfront? Negotiate monthly or stagger payments to align with peak revenue months (typically Jan, Sep, when fitness resolutions drive joins).

- **Staffing: benchmark against 40% of revenue.
